warrantyBattery: Data unavailable: Aston Martin USA has not published a separate high-voltage battery warranty for the Valhalla as of 2026-05. The 6.1 kWh battery is covered under the basic vehicle warranty by default; US federal regulation (49 CFR 579) does not require the 8yr/100k mi PHEV/BEV traction-battery warranty floor for vehicles in this class (the requirement applies to vehicles certified as Advanced Technology PZEV/ZEV, which the Valhalla is not). Source: https://www.astonmartin.com/en-us/models/valhalla
infotainment: Aston Martin in-house infotainment with 10.25 in central touchscreen and 10.25 in digital instrument cluster
adasStandard: Standard ADAS suite includes adaptive cruise control with stop-and-go, lane-keep assist, traffic sign recognition, blind-spot monitoring with rear cross-traffic alert, automatic emergency braking with pedestrian detection, and driver attention monitoring. Specifics for the Valhalla unconfirmed by Aston Martin USA brochure; ADAS hardware is shared with DB12/Vantage/DBX architecture. Sources: https://www.astonmartin.com/en-us/models/valhalla ; https://www.astonmartin.com/en-us/models/brochures/valhalla-brochure-2025
adasOptional: Data unavailable: Aston Martin has not published an a-la-carte ADAS options list for the Valhalla as of 2026-05. Reviews indicate the Valhalla is positioned as a track-focused hypercar with a minimal ADAS overlay relative to GT models. Sources: https://www.motor1.com/reviews/791442/aston-martin-valhalla-first-drive-review/
rearViewCameraNotes: Standard high-resolution rearview camera with dynamic guidelines, integrated into the central 10.25 in touchscreen. Required by FMVSS 111 (US rearview-visibility regulation) for all passenger vehicles. Multi-angle and rear-cross-traffic alert imagery available. Source: https://www.astonmartin.com/en-us/models/valhalla
sideViewCameraNotes: Data unavailable: Aston Martin USA brochure and press materials do not confirm surround-view 360 cameras or Honda LaneWatch-style side cameras on the Valhalla; reviews note camera-based rear-view mirrors are NOT fitted (conventional mirrors are used) and side-view monitoring relies on radar-based blind-spot warning rather than dedicated cameras. Source: https://www.astonmartin.com/en-us/models/valhalla
subscriptionFeatures: Connected Car Services subscription (remote lock/unlock, vehicle locator, app integration, OTA delivery) — complimentary 3 years, annual subscription thereafter; price not publicly disclosed. Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are not subscription-gated. No subscription-locked horsepower, heated seats, or ADAS features identified on Valhalla, in contrast to BMW and Mercedes-EQ practices. Source: https://www.astonmartin.com/en-us/legal/am-connected-car-system-terms-and-conditions
drmNotes: The Valhalla operates fully without internet connectivity — propulsion, transmission, ADAS, and infotainment local functions do not require a cellular/Wi-Fi link. Connected Car Services (remote lock/unlock, vehicle location, OTA software, app pairing) require the embedded modem and are complimentary for 3 years from warranty start; after 3 years, owners must subscribe at the prevailing annual rate to retain remote/app features. No reports of Aston Martin remotely disabling propulsion or features post-sale. Sources: https://www.astonmartin.com/en-us/legal/am-connected-car-system-terms-and-conditions ; https://www.astonmartin.com/en-us/legal/aston-martin-connected-car-system-privacy-policy
killSwitchNotes: No impaired-driving-detection kill switch is present in MY2026 Valhalla; the federal IIJA-driven NHTSA mandate has not yet finalized rulemaking. The Valhalla includes driver-attention monitoring (eye/face tracking via a camera in the steering column) that issues warnings but does not disable the vehicle. Source: https://www.kbb.com/car-news/nhtsas-new-kill-switch-law-approaches-key-deadline/
knownIssues: Data unavailable: As a 2026 inaugural-year model with first deliveries beginning December 2025, no statistically meaningful owner-issue dataset exists as of 2026-05. Aston Martin's broader portfolio (Mercedes-AMG-shared powertrains) historically shows infotainment glitches and electrical gremlins as the most common owner complaints. Source: https://www.jdpower.com/cars/ratings/aston-martin
recalls: Data unavailable: No NHTSA recalls have been issued for the MY2026 Aston Martin Valhalla as of 2026-05. Source: https://www.nhtsa.gov/recalls
stateIncentives: Data unavailable: As an exotic PHEV with MSRP ~$1M and AGI/MSRP caps in CA CVRP, NY Drive Clean Rebate, NJ Charge Up, MA MOR-EV, and CO Innovative Motor Vehicle Credit all exclude it. The Valhalla does not qualify for the federal Section 30D Clean Vehicle Credit (MSRP cap $80k for SUV/vans, $55k for sedans/cars — the Valhalla exceeds both, and Aston Martin does not have a US final-assembly plant). Source: https://www.fueleconomy.gov/feg/tax2023.shtml
